This view of the matter, at any rate, puts it out of all doubt that the supposed abolition of the 배심 재판, by the operation of this provision, is fallacious and untrue. The 입법부 of 합중국 would certainly have full power to provide, that in appeals to the Supreme Court there should be no re-examination of facts where they had been tried in the original causes by juries. This would certainly be an authorized exception; but if, for the reason already intimated, it should be thought too extensive, it might be qualified with a limitation to such causes only as are determinable at common law in that mode of trial.

The amount of the observations hitherto made on the 권위 of the judicial department is this: that it has been carefully restricted to those causes which are manifestly proper for the cognizance of the national judicature; that in the partition of this 권위 a very small portion of original 관할권 has been preserved to the Supreme Court, and the rest consigned to the subordinate 법정s; that the Supreme Court will possess an appellate 관할권, both as to law and fact, in all the cases referred to them, both subject to any exceptions and regulations which may be thought advisable; that this appellate 관할권 does, in no case, abolish the 배심 재판; and that an ordinary degree of prudence and integrity in the national councils will insure us solid advantages from the establishment of the proposed 사법부, without exposing us to any of the inconveniences which have been predicted from that source.

2. This power has been absurdly represented as intended to abolish all the county courts in the several States, which are commonly called inferior courts. But the expressions of the Constitution are, to constitute "법정s INFERIOR TO THE SUPREME COURT"; and the evident design of the provision is to enable the institution of local courts, subordinate to the Supreme, either in States or larger districts. It is ridiculous to imagine that county courts were in contemplation.
3. This word is composed of JUS and DICTIO, juris dictio or a speaking and pronouncing of the law.
4. I hold that the States will have concurrent 관할권 with the subordinate federal judicatories, in many cases of federal cognizance, as will be explained in my next paper.
From McLEAN's Edition, New York. Wednesday, May 28, 1788

THE erection of a new 정부, whatever care or wisdom may distinguish the work, cannot fail to originate questions of intricacy and nicety; and these may, in a particular manner, be expected to flow from the establishment of a 헌법 founded upon the total or partial incorporation of a number of distinct sovereignties. 'Tis time only that can mature and perfect so compound a system, can liquidate the meaning of all the parts, and can adjust them to each other in a harmonious and consistent WHOLE.

Such questions, accordingly, have arisen upon the plan proposed by the convention, and particularly concerning the 사법부 department. The principal of these respect the situation of the State courts in regard to those causes which are to be submitted to federal 관할권. Is this to be exclusive, or are those courts to possess a concurrent 관할권? If the latter, in what relation will they stand to the national 법정s? These are inquiries which we meet with in the mouths of men of sense, and which are certainly entitled to attention.

The principles established in a former paper(1) teach us that the States will retain all pre-existing authorities which may not be exclusively delegated to the federal head; and that this exclusive delegation can only exist in one of three cases: where an exclusive 권위 is, in express terms, granted to the Union; or where a particular 권위 is granted to the Union, and the exercise of a like 권위 is prohibited to the States; or where an 권위 is granted to the Union, with which a similar 권위 in the States would be utterly incompatible. Though these principles may not apply with the same force to the 사법부 as to the legislative power, yet I am inclined to think that they are, in the main, just with respect to the former, as well as the latter. And under this impression, I shall lay it down as a rule, that the State courts will retain the 관할권 they now have, unless it appears to be taken away in one of the enumerated modes.
